exercise‐induced atrial and ventricular tachyarrhythmias can occur in patients with left ventricular non‐compaction and normal systolic function.

we found that a 12-lead ECG is useful in the diagnosis of LVNC, and that the presence of a QRS complex with a left bundle branch block pattern and a prolonged duration (≥ 110 ms) is associated with a high probability of LVNC.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a case with exercise induced ventricular and atria tachycardies.
exercise‐induced atrial and ventricular tachyarrhythmias in patients with normal left ventricular systolic function may be caused by isolated left ventricular myocardial noncompaction.

exercise‐induced atrial and ventricular tachyarrhythmias in a patient with left ventricular non‐compaction and normal ejection fraction are not uncommon, and the mechanism is most likely focal atrial tachyarrhytmias.
The main takeaway from our work is that
exercise‐induced atrial and ventricular arrhythmias in a patient with normal ejection fraction should raise the suspicion of noncompaction cardiomyopathy.

isolated left ventricular (LV) noncompaction (LVNC) can be associated with exercise‐induced ventricular and atria tachycardiac (VT and AT) and should be considered in the differential diagnosis of catecholaminergic ventricular tachyarrhythmias.
exercise‐induced ventricular arrhythmias in patients with normal left ventricular function should not be automatically attributed to catecholaminergic ventricular tachyarrhythmias.
